body:
## Problem

Known limit of the #593 fix (PR #619, "Known limits"): the hold of an unpublished bundle does not always cascade. `template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:712-713` (branch `fix/593-stack-mode-append-only-fold-real-base-prs`) skips a direct dependent D of a held bundle U, but does not add D to `held`. The cascade relies on D never reaching COMPLETE. If D was already COMPLETE on disk when the run started (a resumed batch), a later E that depends on D passes `_runnable` and builds on a line that has neither U nor D.

The not-COMPLETE skip already had this narrow gap; the new `held` path inherits it. Brief (iv) of #593 requires the hold to cascade "through another" bundle. Raised as `[impl]` by the final code review and accepted at sign-off without a rebuild.

## Done when

Every bundle `_runnable` skips for a held prerequisite is added to the held set (or `held` is checked through the whole dependency chain). A flow test pins U (held) → D (COMPLETE before the run) → E: E is skipped and named.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 final code review + PR #619 Known limits).
title: stack mode: the hold of an unpublished bundle does not cascade through a dependent that was already COMPLETE before the run
